suggestions.assertion: Every reported problem cites a specific file and line
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating; passes in all four runs, with the same absence-finding exceptions everywhere.

Nothing in the assertion set penalises volume. This run reported 15 findings including three Minor nits (sequential await, undocumented timeout override, doc-comment tone) that a merge-gate reviewer would arguably drop. Signal-to-noise is a real differentiator between runs and is currently unmeasured — a finding-count or precision assertion would capture it.

No assertion checks whether the review names the *rule* (reviewer-core takes an injected LLMProvider and does no I/O) versus merely spotting the symptom. All four runs name it, but only because they all read reviewer-core/CLAUDE.md — worth an explicit assertion if that grounding is what the skill is meant to guarantee.

eval_feedback.overall: 5/5, same as every other run in this iteration. The assertion set is saturated: it cannot separate these four outputs. Differentiation must come from finding counts, precision, and decoy handling.
